page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on external premium storage options.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ls_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score of 68669.54 and a PassMark CPU score of 87182.31. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2235.58. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 5133.04 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 326.02 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, contribute to strong performance in specialized workloads, such as a static web serving throughput of 89.08 GB/sec and a Redis SET throughput of 113.0 million operations per second.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D64ls_v7 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local storage. This makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive in-memory databases or local scratch disks. It is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and CPU-based machine learning inference, as evidenced by its strong prompt processing speeds across various model sizes.

Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, it features 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a lean 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, prioritizing raw CPU compute density. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 87182.31 and a static web serving throughput of 89.08 GB/sec. It also exhibits strong performance in multi-threaded decompression and Redis operations. The D64ls_v7 is highly cost-efficient for compute-intensive tasks that do not demand large memory footprints, making it an excellent fit for high-throughput web serving, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
